response.reconstructed_markdown:
In India, as globally, the standard reference ranges for blood sugar levels 2 hours after a meal \(known as a 2\-hour postprandial or 2\-h PG test\) depend on whether a person has diabetes. According to bodies like the [Research Society for the Study of Diabetes in India \(RSSDI\)](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESTwHrOzAVgx32bi9AQFFAaQ6rWihqtlXAyC_8v1Ubfc9zhr0hqXVrfi89pMARGdBU0EC6vQQ9Qpd91r3x47kKte1x2GGeWzetu_E2MDwRMM8), the standard thresholds are: [0]

- Normal \(Non\-diabetic\): Less than 140 mg/dL \(7.8 mmol/L\).
- Prediabetes \(Impaired Glucose Tolerance\): 140 to 199 mg/dL \(7.8 to 11.0 mmol/L\).
- Diabetes Mellitus: 200 mg/dL \(11.1 mmol/L\) or higher. [1] [2] [3]

If you are already managing diabetes, the goals are slightly higher to prevent hypoglycemia \(low blood sugar\): [0] [4]

- General Management Target: Less than 180 mg/dL \(and RSSDI guidelines often suggest striving closer to <160 mg/dL post\-meal if it can be achieved safely without low blood sugar episodes\). [2] [4]

If you'd like to share your specific test result or whether you are monitoring for diabetes screening, I can help provide more context or suggest what next steps to discuss with a healthcare provider on Lupi Diagnostics.
